primitives.assumptions: Employer communication delays impact procedural fairness; temporal proximity of events affects evidentiary weight.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When t_{msg} > t_{hearing} - 2 working days, evidentiary integrity is compromised.

primitives.name: Evidentiary Sufficiency
primitives.verbatim_quote: Since the employer failed to meet the two working days suggestion in sending me the evidence, I believe it's only fair to allow this information into submission as well.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E_{submitted}': 'evidence submitted by employee (dimensionless)', 'E_{required}': 'evidence required by tribunal guidelines (dimensionless)', 'T_{delay}': 'time delay in evidence delivery (days)'}
primitives.assumptions: Procedural fairness requires timely evidence; delayed submissions must be considered under equal access conditions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If T_{delay} > 2 working days, E_{submitted} may be deemed insufficient without justification.

layer2.mapping: Evidentiary sufficiency is derived from the temporal kernel of communication delay and procedural adherence.
layer2.telemetry: Ratio of submitted vs required evidence within temporal window

primitives.name: Procedural Fairness
primitives.verbatim_quote: Although it is suggested by TWCthat "documents should be receieved at least two working days prior to the scheduled hearing," and not required.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_{fair}': 'measure of procedural fairness (dimensionless)', 'D_{doc}': 'document delivery time (days)', 'T_{hearing}': 'hearing start time (days)'}
primitives.assumptions: Fairness is quantified by adherence to recommended timelines; deviation implies potential bias.
primitives.breakdown_regime: F_{fair} = 1 if D_{doc} ≤ T_{hearing} - 2 working days, else F_{fair} < 1.

layer2.mapping: Procedural fairness is derived from the temporal distance between document receipt and hearing.
